title: What they said at the time

clips.q: Coors Brewing Co. of Golden, Colorado, is testing a clear malt beverage, called Zima in three markets.
clips.who: **The Washington Post**, March 1993, as quoted in a 2017 column[^25]
**David Letterman**, No. 9 of “The Top Ten Signs Your U.S. Senator Is Nuts,” as quoted by Westword[^12]

clips.q: Our trial curve was so huge we almost hit 1.3 million barrels last year.
clips.who: **Mark Lee**, Zima brand manager, Westword, Sep 6, 1995[^12]

clips.q: The consumer is young and will move on to the next product. Zima had its peak; now Coors needs to rekindle interest.
clips.who: **Michael Bellas**, Beverage Marketing Corporation, Westword, Sep 6, 1995[^12]

clips.q: Unfortunately, the success of this product was not as expected and the product was withdrawn later in the year.
clips.who: **Adolph Coors Company**, 10-K for 1995, on Zima Gold[^3]

clips.q: Rarely has such a famously maligned product enjoyed such a lengthy run.
clips.who: **Slate**, “The Long, Slow, Torturous Death of Zima,” Nov 26, 2008[^13]

clips.q: In Japan it’s not embarrassing at all to be caught drinking Zima.
clips.who: **Kayoko Okochi**, Molson Coors Japan brand manager, The Daily Beast, Sep 2014[^29]

clips.q: If you’re one of the zillion fans who have missed Zima, the answer should be clear.
clips.who: **Marty Maloney**, MillerCoors spokesman, Chicago Tribune, Feb 17, 2017[^23]

clips.q: Whether you remember it or not, this summer is your only chance to taste the ‘it’ drink of the ’90s.
